summary.headline: Hindustan Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 33% YoY to INR42.8 crore, a record, while footwear cost pressure of ~INR6 crore weighed; FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Total income rose 18% YoY to INR1,207 crore and EBITDA rose 26% to INR106.3 crore, with PBT up 33% to INR56.6 crore. Footwear absorbed about INR6 crore of raw material, freight and minimum-wage cost pressure, with the Haryana wage hike the main driver. Management reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore and announced INR190 crore of new projects, taking FY27 commitments to INR340 crore plus INR150 crore carried forward. A Silvassa plant disruption from July rains is expected to be fully resolved by end-August.

financial_highlights.metric: Footwear cost pressure (raw material, freight, wages)

segments.name: Home & Personal Care
segments.commentary: Running at maximum capacity with a record quarter; Aurangabad personal care integration complete. Silvassa brownfield expected to start in Q2 FY27 and Lucknow greenfield later this year. INR50 crore Lucknow project (bar and liquid lines) announced.

segments.name: Food & Beverages
segments.commentary: Coimbatore, Nashik and Mysuru at record production; beverages had an excellent season. INR210 crore of beverage projects across Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad, expected online by Dec/Jan. Greek yogurt facility being added in Goa.

segments.name: Ice Cream
segments.commentary: Strong summer with record volumes; Panipat facility commissioned in Q1. INR80 crore Panipat expansion announced; Nashik cone and ice cream utilisation improving with new customers.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Q1 utilisation was poor due to imported material and freight disruption, and cost pressure hit margins. Management says utilisation is about 80-90% from August; order book full from Q2 FY27 and the business is expected to pay off in H2 FY27. Price pass-through now being achieved from Q1 onward per management.

segments.name: Healthcare / OTC Pharma
segments.commentary: Baddi site approved; commercial production started for 2 more multinational companies. Management expects Baddi to reach 100% utilisation within 6-12 months. Class III medical device certification started at Chennai.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore reaffirmed; management said it is too early to signal the lower end and will revisit in a couple of quarters.
Capacity commercialisation of more than INR500 crore expected in FY27 including carry-forward projects.
Management expects footwear to return to profitability in coming months and to pay off in H2 FY27.
Profit growth expected to outpace revenue growth because customers increasingly supply raw and packing material, so only conversion cost is booked as revenue.
Continued 1:1 debt-equity funding for projects; growth to rely on internal accruals with ROCE threshold of 18%.
capex_capacity: FY27 new project commitments of INR340 crore (INR190 crore newly authorised), plus INR150 crore carried forward from FY26.
Breakdown: Food & Beverages INR210 crore; Ice Cream INR80 crore (Panipat); Home & Personal Care INR50 crore (Lucknow).
Silvassa flood disruption from July rains: partially restored, fully operational by end-August; management says it is insured and has no material long-term impact.
Lucknow greenfield facility due for commissioning later in FY27; Silvassa brownfield to start in Q2 FY27.
Pipeline of inquiries about INR1,000 crore, not yet confirmed; policy is to announce capex only after signing.
demand_pricing: Footwear raw material prices rose ~50-60% (polymer, fabric) and freight rose up to 4x; footwear pricing is fixed 6-12 months ahead, so costs could not be passed through in Q1.
Haryana/NCR minimum wage hike of ~30% hit footwear and was described as a local, one-off issue; other contracts have pass-through clauses.
Footwear order book full for Q2 FY27 onward, with new domestic and multinational customer wins and some lapsed customers returning.
HPC demand has improved materially over the last three months per management, with liquid home care volumes growing near double digits.
US personal care order is on hold due to tariff ambiguity and freight; product development, trials and mould investment are complete.
Middle East export discussions (UAE, Saudi Arabia) put on hold; Dr. Scholl portfolio exported to UK, EU, Australia, NZ and Japan.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company negotiate better terms with customers given GST inversion and weakening competition, and is there any asset revaluation planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sameer Kothari said GST inversion is not the main driver of outsourcing and that the company is better placed to handle it. Assets have not been revalued and the business model does not depend on it; the value sits on the balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Can footwear raw-material cost increases be built into contracts structurally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shoe contracts are set 6-8 months ahead with fixed prices, so mid-season changes are not industry practice. Brands have agreed to absorb some cost for the coming season, and pass-through is now being achieved.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the INR340 crore of new projects by segment.
qa_highlights.answer: Food & Beverages INR210 crore across five units, Ice Cream INR80 crore at Panipat, and HPC INR50 crore at Lucknow for a bar and liquid line.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear utilisation and order book quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 utilisation was poor; utilisation is about 80-90% from August with a full order book and new logos, with the business expected to pay off in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Footwear employee cost share and profit impact of INR210 crore beverage capex at 18% ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Footwear employee cost is about 35-40% of Q1 total. Beverage units are expected online by Dec/Jan on anchor-tenant basis; the analyst's ROCE maths was corrected to EBIT, with 1:1 debt-equity funding implying interest outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block growth outlook over 3-5 years versus sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross block will grow faster than sales because customer-supplied raw material means only conversion cost is booked as revenue. It expects to fund growth from internal accruals at 1:1 leverage with an 18% ROCE threshold.

risks_watch: Footwear margin recovery depends on brands absorbing cost and on Middle East-driven material and freight costs easing; ~INR6 crore hit in Q1.
Silvassa restoration by end-August and insurance recovery; watch for any Q2 output shortfall.
Execution of INR500 crore capex this year, and whether Lucknow and Silvassa start on time.
US tariff ambiguity keeps personal care export orders on hold.
Management declined to give plant-level utilisation for shared sites; footwear ROCE is below the 18% threshold, per management.
key_quotes: we delivered our highest ever quarterly PAT with a growth of nearly 1/3, 33% over last year.
we are confident that our customers will support us in mitigating the losses incurred due to these causes and that the division will return to profitability in the coming months.
I think it's too early to say that, Virat. We have continued to reaffirm our guidance.
I think the shoe business should finally start paying off in the second half of this financial year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core business and FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crore, which was reaffirmed. Cautious and somewhat defensive on footwear: it is described as temporarily stressed, management repeatedly declined to give plant-level utilisation or category EBITDA, and it was reluctant to say GST inversion is a tailwind or to give a hit ratio on the project pipeline.
